glossary_terms.meaning: A SKILL.md, *.agent.md or *.prompt.md file, the three kinds validate_agent_files discovers.
The caller-supplied basenames (default: test, tests, caches, .git, node_modules) pruned only outside a git work tree.
Markdown a plugin ships besides its catalog entry files (references/ pages, the plugin README), checked for references only.
A JSON object colocated with the directory it describes, one top-level key per consuming tool.
A metadata key, such as template-consume, that is valid only in the repository-root metadata file.
A warning-level skill finding shown only with --recommend; it never changes validity or the exit code.

worst_drift: The Rationale describes per-directory metadata resolution (root-to-leaf walk, accumulation, directory-relative globs) that no code in the checkout implements.
verdict: Seven of eight requirements restate tested loader behaviour, so the loss would be the git-is-the-one-ignore-authority decision and the .agent.metadata.json convention, which has a single implementing consumer and is otherwise recorded nowhere live.

glossary_terms.meaning: An image (agentdev-base) with tools and the staged catalog but no agentdev_runtime package, supervisor, or lifecycle commands.
The service graph PID 1 selects through AGENTDEV_RUNTIME_MODE: deploy or devcontainer.
The three Dev Container lifecycle commands agentdev-runtime lifecycle created, ready, attached, each with its own hook directory.
The agentdev plugin catalog copied into the image at AGENTDEV_CATALOG_DIR (/opt/agentdev), used unless the checkout ships a complete one.
A failure the controller cannot recover; deploy waits for supervisor retry, a Dev Container exits nonzero.
A supervised program (OpenCode, Remote Control, docker-gc) that starts after the create phase and never gates readiness.
/etc/agentdev/hooks/{created,started,attached}.d/, image-installed executables run in C-locale order at the end of a phase.
Consuming the whole template through /agentdev:template-consume, as opposed to only referencing the published image.

worst_drift: Requirement 'lifecycle phases remain distinct' forbids create-once work in the entrypoint, while docker/devcontainer/supervisord.conf#program:created runs the create phase under PID 1 and postCreateCommand only waits — the same spec's 'non-root account' requirement and 'PID 1 owns the create phase' rationale describe the real behaviour.
verdict: Lost: fifteen rationale entries (about eleven ADR-worthy, 25 rejected alternatives) that some twenty code comments point at by spec key, and the only statement of three untested contracts (the PPA republisher's verification, the host-side extra-CA handover, gh PATH precedence); the other requirements are already executable tests or self-evident Dockerfile and Ansible text.

glossary_terms.meaning: A review by plume-works-quill[bot] in state approved, changes_requested, or commented, on any commit of the pull request.
The required gate job that passes when an accepted review exists or the author is a trusted bot.
The claude-respond job, check name 'Claude PR Review Responder', that runs Claude with the pr-review skill.
The job that excludes forks and bot authors, authorizes the event actor, reads labels live, and decides whether a review runs.
A Bot login listed in TRUSTED_BOT_ACTORS whose pull requests are approved by the App instead of reviewed.
Label that requests a review; the review job removes it when the review finishes.
Label that stops every review on a pull request without waiving the gate.
The GitHub App that is the only automated reviewer and approver.

inbound_use: .github/workflows/ai-responder.yml (seven comments reading "see spec/ai-review-gate" in place of the reason)
worst_drift: The spec, its Rationale, and README.md#pull-request-automation say the gate is pending while a review runs; docs/knowledge/data/findings/rereview-gate-pending.md#measurement found a re-review of an already-gated head keeps showing the earlier pass, so a merge need not wait. In code, the trusted-bot approval job has no actor authorization although the spec says no responder job acts for an actor without write access.
verdict: Lost: 25 rejected alternatives across seven decisions, the only one-place statement of a trigger and label lifecycle whose implementation is untested inline workflow JavaScript, the only record of the GitHub settings the workflow assumes (main ruleset, environment secrets, App installation), and the target of eleven code comments that defer their reason to this spec.

glossary_terms.meaning: The head commit together with the title and description a review run read when it started; the unit a review covers.
The later of the last description edit and the last title rename; only runs started after it count.
request-ai-review still on the pull request with no unfinished ai-responder run on the head branch to take it.
The AI reviewer's latest APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED review; a later COMMENTED review does not replace it.
The run a push to an already-reviewed pull request starts, whose responder check is skipped.
pr-open run on a branch that already has an open pull request.
pr-review's stop when the title or description misdescribes the diff.

worst_drift: none
verdict: Lost: five rejected alternatives and one recorded gap (update-branch pushes a judgment-call conflict merge with no re-review evaluation); every behaviour is carried by request-review.py with 33 tests and by four SKILL.md files.

glossary_terms.meaning: The read-only copy of .claude-plugin/ and .agents/plugins/ the image build places at $AGENTDEV_CATALOG_DIR (/opt/agentdev).
A root holding .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and the OpenCode bridge directory, so it may replace the staged catalog.
The plugin directory .agents/plugins/agentdev/.opencode-plugin, registered in the `plugin` list of the user's opencode.json.

glossary_terms.term: create phase / start phase / attach phase
glossary_terms.meaning: The three `agentdev-runtime lifecycle created|ready|attached` commands a Dev Container runs once per container, per start, and per editor attach.
The per-instance agentdev-home-${devcontainerId} volume mounted at /home/agent; it starts empty and shadows what the image wrote there.
The volume named after the host user's UID and GID, mounted at /var/lib/agentdev/auth, that holds only Claude credentials.
The per-worktree Claude marketplace registered from <worktree>/.claude/marketplace.local.json.
The agentdev-deploy image, whose supervisor runs `workspace prepare` and `workspace config` instead of the Dev Container lifecycle commands.

glossary_terms.meaning: A file under the agentdev plugin's bin/ or a skill's agent-code/ directory that an agent or user runs.
A skill's directory of bundled executable code, named so instead of the Agent Skills convention scripts/.
result_codes.py, skill_common.py and the other modules in the plugin bin/ that skill scripts import through sys.path.
The directory a host installs the plugin into in a consuming repository; scripts run from there, not from this checkout.
The exit-code and last-stdout-line convention the skill-scripts skill defines for every skill script.
skill_common's reproduction of bash's printf %q.

glossary_terms.meaning: A workflow job on a bare GitHub runner rather than inside the agentdev-devcontainer image.
The environment is synced by uv and reached only through `uv run`; no step exports VIRTUAL_ENV or edits PATH.

glossary_terms.meaning: A `uses:` starting with `$/`, which loads an action or reusable workflow from this repository at the running commit without a checkout.
The head commit of the calling workflow's last successful push run on the base branch.
The shared composite action whose `image` filter decides whether a workflow's real jobs run.
The branch the paths-filter action treats as the push target, `main` by default.

duplicates: .github/actions/paths-filter/action.yml › "diff from the last commit this workflow passed on instead"
scripts/tests/test_paths_filter_last_pass.py › "Tests that a push to main is filtered against the last commit its workflow passed on."

glossary_terms.meaning: Remote Control as one tmux pane that resumes a single stored conversation; the default.
`claude remote-control` running as a spawn-on-demand server, selected by `AGENTDEV_CLAUDE_RC_MODE=server`.
Where a server-mode conversation runs: its own git worktree (`worktree`) or the workspace folder (`same-dir`).
The session-mode tmux pane, `agentdev-runtime remote-control session`, bound to the stored conversation ID.
The `SessionStart` hook `agentdev-runtime remote-control pin`, passed only to the pane, that rewrites the stored conversation ID.
The name of both the dedicated tmux server socket and the tmux session that hosts Remote Control.
The create-phase edit of Claude's state files that answers onboarding, trust, Remote Control and project-MCP prompts ahead of time.
A `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` login, which cannot run Remote Control and is kept out of the Claude process.

glossary_terms.meaning: A Claude Code session that runs on a hosted machine with `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`, not on the user's computer.
The machine a cloud session runs on; the checkout and toolchain live on its disk and no devcontainer runs.
The session's loopback HTTPS proxy that injects GitHub credentials and scopes access to the session's repositories.
`.claude/agent-proxy-relay.py`, a TCP forwarder from the Docker bridge address `10.213.0.1:3128` to the agent proxy's changing loopback port.
A reboot of the session host that keeps the disk and stops every process, including `dockerd`, the relay and all containers.
The two modes of `.claude/startup.py`: one-time host provisioning, and the `SessionStart` hook that restores Docker and the relay.

duplicates: .claude/README.md › "The cloud environment runs `startup.py` as its setup script"

The rationale rejects judging GitHub access by `gh auth status`, a credential helper or the bare `github.com` root, while `doctor.py::auth` and `doctor.py::network` run those three checks, and its 401 differs from the 403 in `.claude/CLAUDE.cloud.md#github-access`.

glossary_terms.meaning: The Coder template (plume-works/coder-ide-baseline) that runs this repository as a Dev Container workspace.
`agentdev-runtime coder start`, the default of the template's `agent_start_script` parameter, run on every Coder agent start.
Values such as GITHUB_TOKEN that Coder puts only in its agent's environment, after `devcontainer up` has finished.

glossary_terms.meaning: A file registered in scripts/refresh-pin-checksums.py::PIN_FILES whose pinned downloads carry a SHA-256 per architecture.
The one command Renovate runs on a branch after its edits: scripts/renovate-post-upgrade.py.
Checksums, lock files, and pre-commit rewrites a version bump implies and Renovate must commit with it.
The checksum-carrying single-binary tools the image installs from ansible/roles/dev_tools/defaults/main.yml.
A new version's checksum is whatever the release asset hashes to on the first download; nothing independent verifies it.
A Renovate option only the self-hosted bot's global config accepts, such as allowedCommands; it comes from RENOVATE_* variables.
The issue Renovate maintains, whose checkboxes a person ticks to request an update or rebase.

.github/workflows/renovate.yml › "A pull request opened with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflows"

glossary_terms.meaning: The nested `dockerd` that the `agentdev-devcontainer` runtime supervises inside the container.
The outer Docker engine of a Coder workspace that runs the Dev Container itself; bounded by another repository's spec.
One run of `agentdev-runtime docker gc`: image prune, build-cache trim, disposable-volume removal.
A volume whose name matches `docker.py::DISPOSABLE_VOLUME`; the only volumes a pass may remove.
A volume holding agent credentials; never matched by the disposable pattern, so never removed.
The supervised non-core client service that runs a pass at start and every `AGENTDEV_DOCKER_GC_INTERVAL` seconds.
An image a pass does not remove; build cache it shares does not count toward the 10 GB limit.
The service graph PID 1 selects by `AGENTDEV_RUNTIME_MODE`: `deploy` or `devcontainer`.

glossary_terms.meaning: The script at `/usr/local/bin/gh` that derives `GH_TOKEN` from the git credential helper and then execs the real `gh`.
The program git asks for HTTPS credentials; here either the host's helper or `gh auth git-credential`.
The Coder workspace (or host) that launches the Dev Container, and the Dev Container inside it.
`agentdev-runtime coder start`, run by the Coder template's `coder_script` each time the Dev Container sub-agent starts.
A per-user value Coder injects into the agent's environment, such as `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
The Dev Container start phase, `agentdev-runtime lifecycle ready`.
The environment saved in `AGENTDEV_KEYRING_ENV_FILE` that lets a process reach the supervised GNOME Keyring.

glossary_terms.meaning: The managed values the runtime sets in the user's OpenCode config on every start: `$schema`, `permission["*"]`, `permission.external_directory["/**"]`, and `experimental.subagent_depth`.
Config keys whose values the runtime overwrites on each start, as opposed to every other key, which it preserves in place.
`agentdev-runtime state agent-policy` / `opencode_config.configure`, run by `agentdev-runtime lifecycle ready` (the Dev Container postStartCommand).
A repository that uses the agentdev images or template for its own project rather than this repository.

glossary_terms.meaning: One Dev Container of one checkout or worktree; Compose's project prefix and `${devcontainerId}` keep its volumes apart from other instances.
The external Docker volume `agentdev-agents-auth-<uid>-<gid>` holding Claude's credentials, shared by every instance of one host user.
The per-instance volume `agentdev-home-${devcontainerId}` mounted over `/home/agent`; it starts empty and holds all other state.
The image's `agent` account (1000:1000) after the devcontainer CLI rewrites its UID and GID to the host user's.
The bootstrap giving an empty mount root to the runtime account, and refusing a populated one another UID owns.
The supervised one-shot `agentdev-runtime lifecycle created`, run once per container after the root bootstrap.
`AGENTDEV_VENV_ROOT`, the directory on the home volume holding one uv environment per checkout directory name, reached through each checkout's `.venv` link.
`scripts/run-root-tests`, which runs the `requires_root` tests as root through `sudo -- env -i` from the runtime account.

glossary_terms.meaning: The file of domain names and the `github-meta` keyword whose resolved IPv4 addresses are the only permitted egress destinations.
An allowlist entry that expands to GitHub's published web, api, and git IPv4 ranges.
The post-apply probe that example.com is blocked and api.github.com answers.

glossary_terms.meaning: The remote-tracking branch a new work branch starts from, `<remote>/main` by default, else the remote's default branch.
`main`, `master`, the branch `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` names, or, when that is unset, the one `gh repo view` reports for the remote's URL.
A feature branch that tracks `<remote>/<name>`, never the base, and is the only place commits are made.
Keeping uncommitted and untracked changes in the working tree across the switch to the new branch, possible only when no changed path differs between HEAD and the base.
Creating the branch in a separate `git worktree` named `<repo>-<branch>` and leaving the current checkout untouched.
The runtime image selected by `AGENTDEV_RUNTIME_MODE=deploy`, which mounts only `/workspaces/project`.
The commit of the stash entry the script created and its current `stash@{n}` position, reported whenever the entry is left in the shared stash stack.
The enum on the last stdout line of every skill script (`PROTECTED_BRANCH`, `CARRY_CONFLICT`, ...) that callers match instead of the exit number.

inbound_use: none (two code comments point at the spec by key for a reason they already state themselves: .pre-commit-config.yaml › "Work lands through pull requests; see spec/git-new-branch" and scripts/renovate-post-upgrade.py › "the guard is for commits: see spec/git-new-branch"; deleting the spec leaves both pointers dangling)
worst_drift: Minor: the spec says a detached-HEAD refusal directs the user to git-new-branch, while git-commit.py::run reports PREFLIGHT_ERROR with 'commit on a feature branch instead'. The spec is also silent on the script's --depends-on mode, which overrides 'starts at the fetched remote base' and lives in spec/stacked-prs.
verdict: One decision would be lost — why the branch is pushed at creation with --no-track (a branch tracking the base makes `git pull` pull the base and pr-open's find-branch-pr.py refuse it as PROTECTED_BRANCH) — plus the single statement that git-commit.py and the no-commit-to-branch hook are two layers of one 'never commit on the default branch' rule; the remaining requirements restate SKILL.md and the script's usage text and are asserted by test_git_new_branch.py and test_git_commit.py.

glossary_terms.meaning: A tag CI repoints per event: edge on main, pr-N, a branch name, or a semver tag; also called an event tag.
The sha-<commit> tag a candidate is published under and that is never repointed.
An image a run built and published by digest before acceptance.
Pointing the moving tags at an accepted candidate digest without rebuilding.
The four images one run builds: ubuntu-ansible, agentdev-base, agentdev-deploy, agentdev-devcontainer.
A root-level Compose override that holds a tag-and-digest reference (devcontainer-compose-pins.yml, opencode-compose-pins.yml).
The wait a push to main spends in a cancellable job before any build starts, so a burst of merges builds once.
The native per-architecture deploy and Dev Container test jobs plus the candidate pre-commit run that gate promotion.

duplicates: devcontainer-compose-pins.yml › "Deliberately kept at the repository root"
opencode-compose-pins.yml › "Kept outside the image-build path filter"

scripts/ci-cooldown.py › "Hold a Primary checks run on main for the cooldown before any build job starts."

docker/ansible/Dockerfile › "Renovate moves only this digest, weekly"
docker/deploy/README.md › "names the image by tag and digest"

glossary_terms.meaning: the blank `.iwe/` plus `docs/knowledge/` workspace shipped under the skill's `assets/`
the two trees bootstrap owns in a target root: `.iwe` and `docs/knowledge`
`<root>/.iwe-bootstrap.txn/`, the owner-marked staging directory a later run discards or completes
filling the blank workspace through `/agentdev:iwe-setup`, a separate operation
the user deciding what to do with existing state bootstrap refuses to touch (`RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`)

glossary_terms.meaning: A branch named `iwe/<slug>/iter-<N>-<phase>` that carries one pull request of a plan's work.
The `N` in a work branch name: the plan's Nth work branch across all phases, counted over local branches, remote branches, and pull requests in any state.
`plan`, `impl`, or `ship`: which stage of a plan's lifecycle a work branch belongs to; it picks only the name's suffix.
A plan key's file name without its `YYYYMMDD-` date prefix.
One of `missing`, `cancelled`, `done`, `complete` (no stage, at least one task checkbox, all ticked), or `incomplete`, read from the working tree.
A plan document's extension-less path relative to the IWE workspace, `data/plans/<YYYYMMDD>-<slug>` or its archived `data/archive/<release>/plans/` form.
The retired `impl/<slug>/iter-<N>` and `ship/<slug>/iter-<N>` branch names, which are never parsed, counted, or migrated.
